what: Wesco is a distributor. It buys electrical gear, wire, data cabling and industrial supplies from manufacturers and delivers them to contractors, utilities and factories, holding the inventory so customers do not have to.
customers: Electrical contractors, utilities, data centre builders, manufacturers and telecom operators across North America.
money: wire, conduit, lighting, controls and automation
data centre cabling, network and security equipment
transformers, meters and broadband gear for utilities
moat: A warehouse and delivery network across thousands of locations, plus supplier relationships that let it stock what a contractor needs the same day. Distribution is a scale business and Wesco is one of the two largest.
risks: A 2.7% net margin leaves almost no cushion if volumes fall
$6.8B of debt, much of it from the Anixter acquisition
Distributors earn well when prices rise and badly when they fall, and copper prices are volatile
opportunities: Analysts see about 37% upside, the widest gap among large distributors
Data centre construction has become a major demand source for its cabling and power business
Utilities are replacing ageing grid equipment, a spending cycle expected to run for years
watch: Organic sales growth by segment and the gross margin, which shows whether price increases are being kept.
